query: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis latest status July 2026 - are attacks on ships continuing or has there been a ceasefire/truce? UKMTO attack incidents in Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman in July 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the summary:

## Key Finding: NO Ceasefire — Attacks Are Continuing

As of the latest available reporting (**July 14–16, 2026**), the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis remains in **active military escalation**:

- **The mid-June US–Iran ceasefire/MOU has collapsed.** Trump declared it "over" (July 8); Iran declared it "void" (July 14).
- **Ship attacks are ongoing** — multiple vessels struck through July (tankers near Limah/Qalhat July 6–7, three vessels July 7, two tankers plus the container ship GFS Galaxy July 13).
- **US naval blockade reinstated July 14**; the US disabled an empty tanker heading to Kharg Island on ~July 15–16 (first vessel disabled since blockade resumed).
- **Iran declared the strait "closed until further notice"** (~July 11) and called it a "red line," retaliating against Gulf states with missiles/drones.
- **At least two seafarers killed** in July attacks (including an Indian seafarer).
- **Traffic collapsed** from 49 ships/day (July 7) to ~25/day (July 12), vs. ~60/day pre-crisis.
- **Oman-mediated diplomacy continues but is stalled** — Iran's FM met his Omani counterpart in Muscat, but major disagreements over strait management remain unresolved.

Note: My primary news database (AskNews) was unavailable due to a subscription issue, so findings are drawn from web search plus WebFetch of the Hormuz Strait Monitor timeline, cross-validated across CNN, NBC, Washington Post, Fox, CBS, France 24, Al Jazeera, UN News, and Wikipedia. The most recent granular details I could confirm extend to July 15–16; I could not find independent reporting dated July 17 itself. Full structured findings with sources and data points have been recorded.

key_facts: NO ceasefire is in effect as of mid-July 2026; the mid-June US-Iran ceasefire/MOU has collapsed and both sides declared it void/over (July 8-14).

Ship attacks are CONTINUING: UKMTO/CENTCOM reported multiple vessel attacks in July (tankers near Limah/Qalhat on July 6-7, three vessels July 7, two tankers July 13, GFS Galaxy container ship July 13).
The US reinstated its naval blockade of Iranian ports on July 14, 2026 (confirmed by CENTCOM July 15).
On July 15-16, the US disabled an empty oil tanker heading toward Kharg Island — the first vessel disabled since the blockade resumed.
Iran formally declared the Strait of Hormuz 'closed until further notice' (~July 11) and called it a 'red line.'
At least two seafarers were confirmed killed in the July attacks (including an Indian seafarer); an earlier UAE tanker strike killed one crew member.
Strait traffic fell from a peak of 49 ships/day (July 7) to ~25 ships/day (July 12), versus a pre-crisis norm of ~60/day.
Oman is mediating (dual-corridor traffic proposal); Iran FM Araghchi met Omani counterpart in Muscat, but talks remain stalled and unresolved.
US conducted large strike packages in July (~80+ on July 7, ~90 July 9-10, ~140 on July 11), and Iran retaliated against Gulf states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan, Oman).
